stem_html: In the equation \(\frac{k}{2}x - 6 = 4 - \frac{3}{2}x\), \(k\) is a constant. If the equation has no solution, what is the value of \(k\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • No solution and infinitely many solutions look the same on the way in. Both require the \(x\) terms to match; only the constants tell them apart, and a student who stops at the matching step answers the other question.
  • The sign of a term that has been moved. The \(x\) term on the right is \(-\frac{3}{2}x\). Reading it as \(+\frac{3}{2}x\) gives \(k=3\), which is the answer most often written down.

Collect the variable on one side: \(\frac{k}{2}x + \frac{3}{2}x = 10\), so \(\left(\frac{k+3}{2}\right)x = 10\).

A linear equation has no solution exactly when the coefficient of \(x\) is 0 while the constant is not. Here \(\frac{k+3}{2} = 0\) gives \(k = -3\), and the equation becomes \(0 = 10\), which is false for every \(x\).

Check that this is not the infinitely-many case: with \(k=-3\) the constant left over is 10, not 0, so no value of \(x\) works. The answer is \(-3\).

stem_html: If \(5(t+2) - 3 = 2(t+9)\), what is the value of \(3t\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The question does not ask for \(t\). Solving correctly and then reporting \(t\) is the single most common way to miss this, and \(\frac{11}{3}\) is sitting there as a choice.
  • The quantity asked for is already the easier one. Isolating \(3t\) takes one step fewer than isolating \(t\), so the extra work is also the wrong work.
  • Distributing the 5 across only the first term. \(5(t+2)=5t+10\); writing \(5t+2\) instead changes the constant and produces \(3t=19\).

Why A is right \(5t + 10 - 3 = 2t + 18\) gives \(5t + 7 = 2t + 18\), so \(3t = 11\). The quantity asked for appears directly when the \(t\) terms are collected on one side.

Why B is wrong This is \(9t\), from multiplying the whole equation by 3 after already having \(3t\).

Why C is wrong This comes from \(5(t+2) = 5t + 2\), which drops 8 from the left side and gives \(3t = 19\).

Why D is wrong This is \(t\), not \(3t\). The arithmetic is right and the question was not read to the end.

stem_html: Line \(\ell\) passes through the points \((-2, 7)\) and \((4, -5)\). What is the \(x\)-intercept of line \(\ell\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The \(y\)-intercept arrives first. Finding \(b\) is a step on the way to the answer, so the number 3 is in hand before the question has been answered, and \((0,3)\) is offered as a choice.
  • Dividing by a negative slope. Setting \(0 = -2x + 3\) gives \(x = \frac{3}{2}\); moving the 3 without changing its sign gives \(-\frac{3}{2}\).
  • Coordinates in the wrong order. An \(x\)-intercept has the form \((x, 0)\); two choices are of the form \((0, y)\) and cannot be \(x\)-intercepts at all.

Why A is wrong \(-2\) is the slope, placed in a coordinate pair. It is neither intercept.

Why B is right The slope is \(\frac{-5-7}{4-(-2)} = \frac{-12}{6} = -2\), so \(y = -2x + b\). Using \((4,-5)\): \(-5 = -8 + b\), so \(b = 3\) and \(y = -2x + 3\). Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(x = \frac{3}{2}\).

Why C is wrong This is the \(y\)-intercept, the value of \(b\) computed on the way to the answer.

Why D is wrong A sign error in the last step. \(0 = -2x + 3\) means \(2x = 3\), not \(2x = -3\).

stem_html: The function \(f\) is linear, \(f(3) = 11\), and \(f(7) = 23\). What is the value of \(f(0)\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The slope is a choice. \(3\) is computed first and is exactly what a rushed reading of “\(f(0)\)” produces.
  • Counting steps instead of using the equation. From \(f(3)=11\), stepping back one unit of slope gives 8, which is \(f(2)\), not \(f(0)\). Three steps are needed, not one.
  • Sign of the backward step. Going from \(x=3\) to \(x=0\) subtracts \(3 \times 3 = 9\); adding it instead gives 20, and mishandling the direction elsewhere produces \(-2\).

Why A is wrong This is \(f(2)\): one step of slope back from \(f(3)\) instead of three.

Why B is wrong A sign error in the backward step; it is \(11 - 9\), not \(-(11 - 9)\).

Why C is right The slope is \(\frac{23-11}{7-3} = 3\). Then \(f(0) = f(3) - 3(3) = 11 - 9 = 2\), which also checks against \(f(7) = 2 + 3(7) = 23\).

Why D is wrong This is the slope, not a value of the function.

stem_html: A tank is being drained. The volume \(V\), in liters, remaining after \(t\) minutes is \(V = 240 - 8t\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number 8 in this context?
choices_json: [{"letter":"A","content":"The tank takes 8 minutes to drain completely.","trap":"solved-wrong-quantity"},{"letter":"B","content":"The tank drains 1 liter every 8 minutes.","trap":"ratio-inverted"},{"letter":"C","content":"The tank held 8 liters before draining began.","trap":"axis-misread"},{"letter":"D","content":"The tank drains at a rate of 8 liters per minute."}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The two constants are interchangeable at a glance. 240 is the starting volume and 8 is the rate; a fast reader assigns whichever number is nearer to the interpretation being tested.
  • Rates invert easily. “8 liters per minute” and “1 liter every 8 minutes” use the same two numbers and describe rates that differ by a factor of 64.
  • Time to empty is a computation, not a coefficient. It is \(240 \div 8 = 30\) minutes, and 8 is offered as though it were the answer to that question.

Why A is wrong The tank empties when \(240 - 8t = 0\), that is at \(t = 30\) minutes. 8 is the rate, not the duration.

Why B is wrong This inverts the rate. It would correspond to \(V = 240 - \frac{1}{8}t\), which would take 1,920 minutes to empty.

Why C is wrong The starting volume is the constant term, 240 liters, found by setting \(t = 0\).

Why D is right The coefficient of \(t\) is the change in \(V\) per unit of \(t\). Each additional minute reduces the volume by 8 liters, so the drain rate is 8 liters per minute.

skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
stem_html: A print shop uses two presses. Press A produces 12 posters per hour and press B produces 18 posters per hour. The shop must produce at least 200 posters, and the presses can run for a combined total of no more than 15 hours. If press A runs for \(a\) hours and press B runs for \(b\) hours, which system of inequalities represents this situation?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "\\(12a + 18b \\ge 200\\) and \\(a + b \\le 15\\)"}, {"letter": "B", "content": "\\(12a + 18b \\le 200\\) and \\(a + b \\ge 15\\)", "trap": "sign-flip"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "\\(12a + 18b \\ge 200\\) and \\(12a + 18b \\le 15\\)", "trap": "unit-mismatch"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "\\(a + b \\ge 200\\) and \\(12a + 18b \\le 15\\)", "trap": "unit-mismatch"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Two constraints, two directions, and it is easy to give both the same one. “At least” is \(\ge\) and “no more than” is \(\le\); a student who fixes on one phrase applies its symbol to both lines.
  • Posters and hours are different quantities. \(12a + 18b\) counts posters, and \(a + b\) counts hours. Any inequality comparing 15 hours to a poster count is dimensionally impossible, and two choices do exactly that.

Why A is right \(12a\) posters from press A plus \(18b\) from press B must be at least 200, and the hours \(a + b\) must be at most 15.

Why B is wrong Both inequality signs are reversed, which would require producing at most 200 posters in at least 15 hours.

Why C is wrong The second inequality compares a poster count with 15 hours. The units do not match, and the constraint on time never appears.

Why D is wrong The first line adds hours and compares them to a poster count; the second compares posters to hours. Both are dimensionally wrong.

skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
stem_html:
The system of equations below has solution \((x, y)\).

\(2x + 3y = 17\)
\(5x - y = 17\)

What is the value of \(2x - y\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The question asks for a combination, not for a variable. Solving the system is necessary here, and stopping at \(x = 4\) or \(y = 3\) is the usual miss.
  • Two 17s invite a shortcut. Subtracting the equations because their right sides match gives \(-3x + 4y = 0\), which is true and is not what was asked.

From the second equation, \(y = 5x - 17\). Substituting into the first: \(2x + 3(5x - 17) = 17\), so \(17x = 68\) and \(x = 4\). Then \(y = 5(4) - 17 = 3\).

Check both equations: \(2(4) + 3(3) = 17\) and \(5(4) - 3 = 17\). Both hold.

Now answer the question that was asked: \(2x - y = 8 - 3 = 5\).

stem_html:
The graph of a line is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. Note that each interval on the \(x\)-axis represents 2 units and each interval on the \(y\)-axis represents 1 unit.

Which equation represents the line?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The two axes are not on the same scale. The line rises 3 gridlines for every 6 it runs, so counting gridlines gives \(\frac{1}{2}\). One horizontal gridline is 2 units, so that run is 12 units and the real slope is \(\frac{1}{4}\).
  • Rise over run, inverted. Taking run over rise turns \(\frac{1}{4}\) into 4, which is offered.
  • The intercept is easy to drop. The line crosses the \(y\)-axis at 1, not at the origin.

Why A is wrong The slope is right and the line does not pass through the origin; at \(x = 0\) the graph shows \(y = 1\).

Why B is right Two points on the line are \((0, 1)\) and \((12, 4)\). The slope is \(\frac{4-1}{12-0} = \frac{1}{4}\) and the \(y\)-intercept is 1.

Why C is wrong This is what the picture looks like if both axes are assumed to have the same scale: 3 gridlines up over 6 across. Each horizontal gridline is 2 units, so the run is 12, not 6.

Why D is wrong Run divided by rise instead of rise divided by run.

stem_html: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{x^2 - 9}{x^2 - x - 6}\) for all values of \(x\) for which the expression is defined?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Cancelling terms instead of factors. Striking the \(x^2\) from top and bottom is not legal and produces choice A, which looks like the answer to a much easier question.
  • The factorization of the denominator has one negative. \(x^2 - x - 6 = (x-3)(x+2)\), not \((x+3)(x-2)\), and the second version is what generates two of the wrong choices.

Why A is wrong This treats \(x^2\) as a common factor and cancels it. Testing \(x = 0\) gives \(\frac{9}{6} = \frac{3}{2}\) by coincidence, but \(x = 1\) gives \(\frac{9}{7}\) against the original's \(\frac{-8}{-6} = \frac{4}{3}\).

Why B is wrong The numerator's factor is kept correctly and the denominator's sign is wrong; at \(x = 0\) this gives \(-\frac{3}{2}\), not \(\frac{3}{2}\).

Why C is right \(x^2 - 9 = (x-3)(x+3)\) and \(x^2 - x - 6 = (x-3)(x+2)\). The common factor \((x-3)\) cancels, leaving \(\frac{x+3}{x+2}\). Checking at \(x = 0\): the original is \(\frac{-9}{-6} = \frac{3}{2}\), and so is \(\frac{3}{2}\).

Why D is wrong This is what comes from factoring the denominator as \((x+3)(x-2)\), which expands to \(x^2 + x - 6\), not the given expression.

stem_html: The equation \((2x + a)(3x + b) = 6x^2 + 19x + 15\) is true for all \(x\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive integers. What is the value of \(a + b\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Two of the choices are numbers printed in the problem. 15 is \(ab\) and 19 is \(2b + 3a\); both are quantities you compute with, and neither is \(a + b\).
  • The middle coefficient is not symmetric. Expanding gives \(2b + 3a\), so \(a = 3, b = 5\) works and \(a = 5, b = 3\) does not. Trying the pair in the wrong order and finding 21 instead of 19 is where the time goes.

Why A is wrong This is \(ab\), the constant term, not the sum.

Why B is wrong This is the middle coefficient \(2b + 3a\), copied from the equation.

Why C is wrong This is the leading coefficient, which is fixed by the 2 and the 3 and carries no information about \(a\) and \(b\).

Why D is right Expanding: \(6x^2 + (2b + 3a)x + ab\). So \(ab = 15\) and \(2b + 3a = 19\). The positive integer pairs for 15 are \((1,15), (3,5), (5,3), (15,1)\), and only \(a = 3, b = 5\) gives \(2(5) + 3(3) = 19\). Then \(a + b = 8\).

stem_html: What is the sum of all solutions to the equation \(\sqrt{2x + 7} = x - 4\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Squaring both sides creates solutions the original equation does not have. The squared equation has two roots, and only one satisfies the equation you were given.
  • “Sum of all solutions” rewards skipping the check. Adding both roots gives 10, which is a choice, and it takes less work than testing them.
  • A square root is never negative. Since the left side is at least 0, the right side must be too, so any solution needs \(x \ge 4\) — which rules out \(x = 1\) before any arithmetic.

Why A is right Squaring gives \(2x + 7 = x^2 - 8x + 16\), so \(x^2 - 10x + 9 = 0\) and \(x = 1\) or \(x = 9\). Testing in the original: at \(x = 9\), \(\sqrt{25} = 5\) and \(9 - 4 = 5\), so it holds. At \(x = 1\), \(\sqrt{9} = 3\) but \(1 - 4 = -3\), so it fails. Only \(x = 9\) is a solution, and the sum is 9.

Why B is wrong This adds both roots of the squared equation without checking them. \(x = 1\) is extraneous.

Why C is wrong This is the extraneous root by itself, and it can be eliminated on sight because \(x - 4\) would be negative.

Why D is wrong 25 is \((x-4)^2\) evaluated at the true solution, an intermediate value rather than a solution.

stem_html: In the equation \(x^2 + kx + 36 = 0\), \(k\) is a positive constant. If the equation has exactly one distinct real solution, what is the value of \(k\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The discriminant gives two values and the problem allows one. \(k^2 = 144\) yields \(\pm 12\), and the condition “\(k\) is a positive constant” is the sentence that decides between them.
  • The square root of the constant term is not \(k\). \(\sqrt{36} = 6\) is the repeated root's magnitude, not the coefficient.

Why A is wrong 72 is \(2 \times 36\), a rearrangement of the constant term rather than a value of \(k\); the discriminant would be \(72^2 - 144\), which is far from 0.

Why B is right One distinct real solution means the discriminant is 0: \(k^2 - 4(1)(36) = 0\), so \(k^2 = 144\) and \(k = \pm 12\). Since \(k\) is positive, \(k = 12\), and the equation factors as \((x+6)^2 = 0\).

Why C is wrong It satisfies the discriminant condition and violates the stated condition that \(k\) is positive.

Why D is wrong 6 is the repeated root's magnitude: the solution is \(x = -6\). The coefficient is twice that.

stem_html: What is the positive difference between the two solutions to the equation \((x - 3)^2 = 49\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Taking only the positive square root. \(x - 3 = 7\) gives one solution; the equation also allows \(x - 3 = -7\), and a student who takes one root has nothing to subtract.
  • The difference of the solutions is not the square root. Answering 7 is the most common miss, and it is half the correct value.

Take both square roots: \(x - 3 = 7\) or \(x - 3 = -7\), so \(x = 10\) or \(x = -4\).

Both check in the original equation: \((10-3)^2 = 49\) and \((-4-3)^2 = (-7)^2 = 49\).

The positive difference is \(10 - (-4) = 14\). Note that this is twice the square root, which is what makes 7 such a tempting wrong answer.

stem_html: The graph of the quadratic function \(f\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. The function can be written in the form \(f(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k\), where \(a\), \(h\), and \(k\) are constants. What is the value of \(a + h + k\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The sign inside the vertex form is subtracted. With vertex \((2, -9)\), \(h = 2\) and \(k = -9\); reading \(h = -2\) from the minus sign in the formula is the standard error and gives \(1-2-9=-10\).
  • Assuming \(a = 1\) without checking. Here \(a\) happens to be 1, but only because the \(x\)-intercepts are 3 units from the vertex and the depth is 9. A student who assumes it is right for the wrong reason will be wrong on the next question of this type.
  • The question asks for a sum, not for the function. Writing \(f(x) = (x-2)^2 - 9\) correctly and then reporting a coefficient is the last place to lose the point.

Why A is wrong This comes from \(h = -2\), reading the sign in \((x - h)\) as part of \(h\).

Why B is wrong 12 is \(9 + 2 + 1\), the same three numbers with the vertex's negative sign dropped.

Why C is right The vertex is \((2, -9)\), so \(h = 2\) and \(k = -9\). The parabola passes through \((-1, 0)\): \(0 = a(-1-2)^2 - 9 = 9a - 9\), so \(a = 1\). Then \(a + h + k = 1 + 2 - 9 = -6\).

Why D is wrong 6 is the correct sum with its sign dropped. \(a+h+k=1+2-9=-6\), and the value asked for is negative.

stem_html: The population of a colony of bacteria is modeled by \(P(t) = 1200(0.85)^t\), where \(t\) is the number of years since the colony was first measured. Which statement best describes the colony?
choices_json: [{"letter":"A","content":"The population decreases by 85% each year.","trap":"percent-wrong-base"},{"letter":"B","content":"The population decreases by 15% each month.","trap":"unit-mismatch"},{"letter":"C","content":"The population decreases by 1,200 each year.","trap":"shortcut-trap"},{"letter":"D","content":"The population decreases by 15% each year."}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The base of an exponential is what remains, not what is lost. 0.85 means 85% is left, so 15% is gone; reading 0.85 as the loss is the standard error.
  • The unit of \(t\) is stated once. \(t\) counts years, and a monthly rate would require a different base entirely.
  • Exponential decay is not a constant subtraction. Choice C describes a linear model, which would be \(P(t) = 1200 - 1200t\) and would reach zero in one year.

Why A is wrong 0.85 is the fraction remaining. An 85% loss each year would be \(P(t) = 1200(0.15)^t\).

Why B is wrong The problem defines \(t\) as years. A 15% monthly decline would leave about 14% of the colony after a year, not 85%.

Why C is wrong 1,200 is the starting population, and the model is multiplicative: the number lost shrinks each year, from 180 in the first year to 153 in the second.

Why D is right Each year the population is multiplied by 0.85, keeping 85% and losing 15%. From 1,200 the first year's population is 1,020, a drop of 180, which is 15% of 1,200.

stem_html: The radius of a right circular cylinder is doubled and its height is halved. The volume of the new cylinder is how many times the volume of the original?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Doubling and halving feel like they cancel. They would if both appeared to the first power. The radius is squared in the volume formula and the height is not, so the two changes are not equal and opposite.
  • Stopping after the radius. Doubling the radius alone multiplies the volume by 4, which is a choice.

Why A is right \(V = \pi r^2 h\). The new volume is \(\pi (2r)^2 \left(\frac{h}{2}\right) = \pi \cdot 4r^2 \cdot \frac{h}{2} = 2\pi r^2 h\), which is twice the original.

Why B is wrong This assumes the doubling and the halving cancel, which would be true only if the volume were proportional to \(r\) rather than to \(r^2\).

Why C is wrong This is the effect of doubling the radius alone, with the change in height not applied.

Why D is wrong This is the effect of halving the height alone.

stem_html: In the \(xy\)-plane, the graph of \(x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 10y = 2\) is a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Completing the square adds to both sides. The constants added on the left to build the squares have to be added on the right as well, and forgetting them is what produces the wrong radii here.
  • \(r^2\) is a choice. 36 is the number that appears at the end of the work, and the question asks for \(r\).
  • The constant on the right is not the radius. Reading 2 as \(r^2\) gives \(\sqrt{2}\) without doing any of the work.

Why A is wrong This comes from subtracting 9 and 25 instead of adding them, giving \(2-34=-32\) and then taking a magnitude, \(\sqrt{32}=4\sqrt{2}\).

Why B is right Complete the square: \(x^2 - 6x + 9\) and \(y^2 + 10y + 25\), adding 9 and 25 to both sides. That gives \((x-3)^2 + (y+5)^2 = 2 + 9 + 25 = 36\), so \(r = 6\).

Why C is wrong 36 is \(r^2\), the right-hand side after completing the square.

Why D is wrong This treats the original right-hand side, 2, as \(r^2\), skipping the two constants that completing the square adds.

stem_html: A sector of a circle has a central angle of \(72^\circ\) and a radius of 10. What is the length of the arc that bounds the sector?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Arc length and sector area use the same fraction and different formulas. \(\frac{72}{360} = \frac{1}{5}\) of the circumference is an arc; \(\frac{1}{5}\) of the area is a region, and 20π is that area.
  • Radius against diameter. Using \(\pi r\) instead of \(2\pi r\) halves the answer to 2π.
  • The angle in radians is not the arc. \(72^\circ = \frac{2\pi}{5}\) radians; the arc is that angle times the radius, not the angle alone.

Why A is wrong This uses \(\pi r\) rather than \(2\pi r\) for the circumference.

Why B is wrong \(\frac{\pi}{5}\) is close to the angle in radians divided by 2; the radius has been left out of the calculation entirely.

Why C is right The sector is \(\frac{72}{360} = \frac{1}{5}\) of the circle. The circumference is \(2\pi(10) = 20\pi\), so the arc is \(\frac{1}{5}(20\pi) = 4\pi\).

Why D is wrong \(20\pi\) is both the full circumference and the sector's area, \(\frac{1}{5}\pi(10)^2\). It is not an arc length.

stem_html: In triangle \(ABC\), the measure of angle \(A\) is \(2x^\circ\), the measure of angle \(B\) is \((x + 20)^\circ\), and the measure of angle \(C\) is \((3x + 10)^\circ\). What is the measure, in degrees, of the largest angle of the triangle?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Solving for \(x\) is the first step, not the answer. \(x = 25\) is a choice, and it is what a student writes down the moment the equation is solved.
  • “Largest” has to be decided after substituting. The largest coefficient is 3, and the angle with it also has a \(+10\); comparing the expressions rather than the values is a habit that fails when the constants differ.
  • Every wrong choice is a real angle of this triangle. Checking that your answer “appears in the problem” cannot distinguish them.

Why A is wrong This is \(x\), not an angle measure.

Why B is wrong This is angle \(A\), which is \(2(25) = 50^\circ\) and not the largest.

Why C is wrong This is angle \(B\), which is \(25 + 20 = 45^\circ\) and is the smallest of the three.

Why D is right The angles sum to 180: \(2x + (x+20) + (3x+10) = 180\), so \(6x + 30 = 180\) and \(x = 25\). The angles are \(50^\circ\), \(45^\circ\) and \(85^\circ\), which sum to 180, and the largest is \(85^\circ\).

stem_html: In right triangle \(ABC\), the right angle is at \(B\), \(\sin(A) = \frac{3}{5}\), and \(AB = 12\). What is the length of \(BC\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • \(AB\) is adjacent to angle \(A\), not the hypotenuse. With the right angle at \(B\), the hypotenuse is \(AC\). Treating the given side as the hypotenuse gives \(\frac{3}{5}(12) = 7.2\), which is offered.
  • The hypotenuse is computed on the way. \(AC = 15\) appears mid-solution and is a choice.
  • Which side is opposite. \(\sin(A)\) compares \(BC\) to \(AC\); using \(\frac{5}{3}\) somewhere in the chain produces 20.

Why A is right The right angle is at \(B\), so \(AC\) is the hypotenuse, \(BC\) is opposite angle \(A\) and \(AB\) is adjacent. From \(\sin(A) = \frac{3}{5}\), \(\cos(A) = \frac{4}{5}\), so \(\frac{AB}{AC} = \frac{4}{5}\) and \(AC = 15\). Then \(BC = \frac{3}{5}(15) = 9\), and \(9\text{-}12\text{-}15\) is a right triangle.

Why B is wrong 15 is \(AC\), the hypotenuse, found on the way to \(BC\).

Why C is wrong This comes from using \(\frac{5}{3}\) in place of \(\frac{3}{5}\) against the 12.

Why D is wrong This is \(\frac{3}{5} \times 12\), which treats \(AB\) as the hypotenuse. The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle, so it is \(AC\).

stem_html: The price of a jacket is increased by 30%. Some weeks later, the new price is decreased by 30%. The final price is what percent of the original price?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The two percentages are taken of different bases. The increase is 30% of the original and the decrease is 30% of the larger price, so the amounts are not equal and they do not cancel.
  • “Up 30, down 30” sounds like zero. That is the answer the question is built to produce, and it is exactly right only when the base does not change.
  • Adding percentages. Treating the changes as \(+30\) and \(-30\) applied additively to 100 gives 100; putting the 9 percent difference on the wrong side of 100 gives 109.

Why A is wrong This subtracts both percentages from 100 as if each were 30% of the original: \(100-30-30=40\).

Why B is right Take the original price as 100. After the increase it is 130. The decrease is 30% of 130, which is 39, leaving 91. As a product: \(1.30 \times 0.70 = 0.91\), so the final price is 91% of the original.

Why C is wrong This assumes the two changes cancel. They would only if the second 30% were taken of the original price rather than of the increased one.

Why D is wrong The product \(1.30\times 0.70=0.91\) is 9% below the original, and this puts the 9% above it instead.

skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
stem_html: A machine fills 4 bottles every 9 seconds. At this rate, how many bottles does the machine fill in 1 hour and 15 minutes?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Two unit conversions, one of them silent. The time has to become seconds before the rate can be used, and 1 hour 15 minutes is 75 minutes, not 1.15 hours.
  • The rate is easy to invert. \(\frac{4}{9}\) bottles per second and \(\frac{9}{4}\) seconds per bottle both look like the given information; multiplying by the wrong one is off by a factor of about 5.

Convert the time: 1 hour 15 minutes is 75 minutes, which is \(75 \times 60 = 4{,}500\) seconds.

The rate is \(\frac{4 \text{ bottles}}{9 \text{ seconds}}\). Multiply: \(4{,}500 \text{ s} \times \frac{4 \text{ bottles}}{9 \text{ s}} = \frac{18{,}000}{9} = 2{,}000\) bottles.

The seconds cancel, which is the check that the rate was used the right way up. The answer is 2000.

skill: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
stem_html: A data set consists of the values 12, 14, 15, 15, 16, and 58. The value 58 is removed from the data set. Which of the following correctly describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices_json: [{"letter":"A","content":"The mean is unchanged and the median decreases.","trap":"mean-vs-median"},{"letter":"B","content":"The mean decreases and the median increases.","trap":"endpoint-off-by-one"},{"letter":"C","content":"The mean decreases and the median is unchanged."},{"letter":"D","content":"Both the mean and the median decrease.","trap":"mean-vs-median"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • An outlier moves the mean and not the median. The median depends on position, and removing the largest value from an even-sized set can leave the middle value exactly where it was.
  • “Removing the biggest number” feels like it must lower everything. It lowers the mean by more than 7, and the median does not move at all.
  • Counting the median of an even set. With six values the median is the average of the third and fourth; with five it is the third. Here both come out to 15, which is what has to be checked rather than assumed.

Why A is wrong This reverses which measure is sensitive to an extreme value. The mean is the one that moves.

Why B is wrong The mean does decrease, and the median does not increase; removing the largest value cannot raise the middle one.

Why C is right Before: the mean is \(\frac{130}{6} \approx 21.7\) and the median is \(\frac{15+15}{2} = 15\). After removing 58: the mean is \(\frac{72}{5} = 14.4\) and the median of 12, 14, 15, 15, 16 is 15. The mean falls by about 7.3; the median is unchanged.

Why D is wrong The median is 15 both before and after, because the repeated 15s sit at the center of the set either way.

stem_html:
The scatterplot shows the relationship between the age of a used tractor, in years, and its resale value, in thousands of dollars, along with a line of best fit. Note that each interval on the vertical axis represents 5 thousand dollars.

Which of the following best describes the slope of the line of best fit?
choices_json: [{"letter":"A","content":"The resale value decreases by about 1 thousand dollars per year of age.","trap":"axis-misread"},{"letter":"B","content":"The resale value decreases by about 5 thousand dollars per year of age.","trap":"axis-misread"},{"letter":"C","content":"The resale value decreases by about 2 years per thousand dollars.","trap":"ratio-inverted"},{"letter":"D","content":"The resale value decreases by about 2 thousand dollars per year of age."}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The vertical gridlines are worth 5, not 1. The line falls about four gridlines over ten years, which counts as 4 if the axis is read as ones and is really 20 thousand dollars.
  • One gridline per two years is not one unit per year. Reading the drop per gridline instead of per unit produces choice B.
  • Slope is value per year here. Choice C inverts the ratio and gives an answer in years per dollar, which no line of best fit on these axes can have.

Why A is wrong This counts gridlines rather than units. The line drops four gridlines, and each one is 5 thousand dollars.

Why B is wrong 5 is the value of one vertical gridline, not the change per year. The line takes about two and a half years to fall one gridline.

Why C is wrong This states the reciprocal, with the axes swapped. The slope of this line is a change in value per year, and reading it the other way round describes a different relationship.

Why D is right The line runs from about \((1, 30)\) to about \((11, 10)\), a drop of 20 thousand dollars over 10 years, so the slope is about \(-2\) thousand dollars per year.

stem_html:
The table summarizes the responses of 90 students to a survey about whether they participate in an after-school program.

YesNoTotal
First-year students181230
Seniors243660
Total424890

If one of the students who responded “Yes” is selected at random, what is the probability that the student is a senior?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The condition sets the denominator. The student is chosen from those who said Yes, so the denominator is 42, not 90 and not 60. Every wrong choice here uses a different denominator.
  • The largest number in the row is not the one you want. Seniors number 60 and 36 of them said No, which makes 60 and 36 attractive and irrelevant.
  • The reversed conditional. \(\frac{24}{60} = \frac{2}{5}\) is the probability that a senior says Yes, which is a different question from the one asked.

Why A is right The Yes column totals 42 students, of whom 24 are seniors. The probability is \(\frac{24}{42} = \frac{4}{7}\).

Why B is wrong \(\frac{24}{60}\) is the probability that a randomly chosen senior said Yes. That reverses the condition.

Why C is wrong \(\frac{24}{90}\) uses the whole survey as the denominator, ignoring the condition that the student said Yes.

Why D is wrong \(\frac{2}{3}\) is \(\frac{60}{90}\), the share of respondents who are seniors, which does not use the Yes column at all.
